name: Auction Forty-Fives
description: Auction Forty-Fives (45s, Nova Scotia style) is a partnership trick game: 4 or 6 players, 5 cards each plus 4-card kitty. Bid in 5s (min 15-20); high bidder declares trump and may exchange with kitty. First team to 120 wins. Trump: 5 highest, then J, then A of hearts (always trump). Each trick 5 points; highest trump in trick +5. Special: 30 for 60 (win all tricks); 60 for 120 when below zero. Part of the Forty-Fives and Spoil Five family; regional rules vary.

history.origins: Descendant of the Irish game Spoil Five; widely played among Irish communities in the New World, especially in Nova Scotia and the rest of Atlantic Canada.
history.cultural: 5 and J high in trump; heart Ace always trump; 120 to win.

setup.players: 4 or 6 in partnerships (opposite). 5 cards each (3+2), 4-card kitty.
setup.deck: 52 cards. Trump: 5 high, then J, A of hearts always trump.
setup.dealing: Left of dealer bids first; dealer may hold. High bidder names trump, may exchange with kitty.

rules.objective: First team to 120 points. Bid in 5s; high bidder declares trump, may use kitty.
rules.gameplay: Follow suit when trump led; else any. Trick = 5 pts; highest trump in trick +5. 30 for 60 = all tricks (60 if made, 30 if not); 60 for 120 only when team below zero. House rules vary.
keyRules: Bid 5s; high bidder declares trump, exchanges with kitty
5 and J high in trump; heart Ace always trump
120 to win; 30 for 60, 60 for 120 special bids

strategy.basic: Bid with trump length and 5s/Jacks; use the kitty to strengthen a hand when you win the auction.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with partner by leading from strength, protect key scoring cards, and avoid overbidding when your team is near game.
strategy.advanced: Track which high trumps (5, J, A♥) have been played, balance risk when bidding 30-for-60 or 60-for-120, and steer the play so that your partnership captures scoring tricks while forcing opponents to waste their trumps.
tips: Bid more aggressively when your hand includes multiple top trumps and solid side-suit winners.
When defending, focus on breaking the bidder's control of trump and stopping them from reaching their contract.
Use score awareness: small contracts are safer when near 120, while high bids make sense when you are far behind.
